extracted.intended_audience: Organizations/offerors preparing and submitting proposals for ONR BAA contracts, cooperative agreements, or other transaction agreements (prime and subrecipients).
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and compliance requirements for preparing, formatting, certifying, and submitting full proposals in response to an ONR Broad Agency Announcement for contracts and other transaction agreements, including administrative, financial, conflict-of-interest, and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 2 CFR Part 170 Appendix A reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities that apply for financial assistance (grants, cooperative agreements or TIAs) as either a prime or sub-recipient under this BAA must provide information in their proposal that describes the necessary processes and systems in place to comply with the reporting requirements identified in 2 CFR Part 170 Appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities are required to meet reporting requirements unless an exception or exemption applies. Refer to 2 CFR Part 170, including Appendix A, for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Assistance Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Assistance Certifications Report is an attestation that the entity will abide by the requirements of the various laws and regulations and the supplemental at Section F.2.iv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must complete the Financial Assistance Certifications as part of SF424 (R&R) block 17 (electronic submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Lobbying and SF-LLL
rubrics_metrics.description: As applicable, submit documentation including SF LLL Disclosure of Lobby Activities and disclosure of any unpaid delinquent tax liability or a felony conviction under any Federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide SF-LLL if applicable; failure to disclose where required may have consequences under federal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding Restrictions on Lobbying (awards > $100,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants, cooperative agreement awards, and TIA awards greater than $100,000 require a certification that no Federal appropriated funds have been or will be paid to influence federal officials in connection with award actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-Federal funds are used to influence, complete and submit SF-LLL. Include the certification language in all subaward documents at all tiers. This certification is material and required by 31 U.S.C. 1352; failure to file may incur civil penalties ($10,000–$100,000 per failure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification re: Prohibition on Internal Confidentiality Agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: By submission, the applicant represents it does not require employees, contractors, or subrecipients seeking to report fraud, waste, or abuse to sign or comply with internal confidentiality agreements or statements that prohibit or restrict lawful reporting to federal investigative or law enforcement personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is checked via SF424 (R&R) block 17 ('I Agree') and subject to penalties for false statements (18 U.S.C. 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification Regarding Disclosure of Funding Sources (Section 223(a) Thornberry NDAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the proposing entity certifies PI and other key personnel current and pending support is current, accurate and complete; agrees to update disclosures upon agency request prior to award and as requested during the award term; and that PI/key personnel are aware of Section 223(a)(1) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checked via SF424 (R&R) block 17; false statements may subject the signer to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (18 U.S.C. 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Codes of Conduct and COI (2 CFR 200.318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to comply with 2 CFR 200.318(c) Codes of Conduct to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in awarding and administering contracts supported by federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You and your organization must disclose any potential or actual scientific or nonscientific conflict(s) of interest, including for any identified subrecipient. The Government may request additional information or a mitigation plan; approval of mitigation plans is at ONR's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Scientific Collaborations in Current and Pending Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborations that occurred prior to submission should be considered when assessing potential conflicts; disclose collaborations and include them in the list of current and pending support for senior/key researchers, even if no formal support was provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of collaborations mitigates potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) Disclosure Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors shall state whether they are aware of any information bearing on the existence of any actual or potential OCI as defined in FAR 2.101 and FAR Subpart 9.5, for themselves and proposed subcontractors/partners/consultants/affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no OCI exists, include an authorized statement certifying none exists. If an OCI exists or the Offeror provides support services to ONR, submit the entity name, contract number(s), description of the OCI, a Mitigation Plan, and a concluding certification. Nondisclosure or misrepresentation may lead to disqualification, termination for default, or other remedial actions (see 18 U.S.C. 1001 and 31 U.S.C. § 3802(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OCI Mitigation Plan Minimum Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Mitigation Plan is required, at minimum it shall provide: organizational charts showing structure related to the BAA and relevant contracts; demonstration of how OCI-creating elements will be isolated; information on geographic/physical separation; processes for reassigning personnel and any restrictions; controls including NDAs over future employment of departing employees; OCI training details (timing, frequency, length, content); and evidence of facts/circumstances asserted to mitigate the OCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise but complete information; the Plan may become part of the contract if accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer Review and Possible OCI Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer will review OCI disclosures and Mitigation Plans and may require more information. If an OCI is found, the Government may impose conditions to avoid conflict, disqualify the Offeror, award with mitigation conditions, or seek a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Contracting Officer determines an actual/significant potential conflict cannot be mitigated, the Offeror is ineligible for award. If accepted, the Mitigation Plan becomes part of the contract. Refusal to disclose required information results in disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review for Basic Research Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals funded as basic research, ONR may use peer reviewers from academia, industry, and Government to appraise performance; peer reviewers not U.S. Govt employees must sign nondisclosure agreements before receiving proposal/report copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic peer reviews monitor quality and inform continued funding decisions. Offerors may include PI travel costs to attend peer review. Reviews may consider information from project or program review meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Equipment/Services (Section 889)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 2 CFR 200.216, 200.471 and Public Law 115-232 section 889, recipients and subrecipients (for awards issued on/after Aug 13, 2020) are prohibited from obligating or expending federal funds to procure, extend/renew contracts for, or enter contracts to procure equipment, services, or systems that use covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial/essential component or critical technology, including equipment produced by Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hikvision, Dahua, or entities owned/controlled by a covered foreign country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibition covers procurement, contract extension/renewal, or entering into contracts for such equipment/services. For implementation, heads of agencies should prioritize funding/technical support to help affected entities transition away from covered equipment/services to replacements and sustain service. See Public Law 115-232 section 889 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Covered Foreign Country
rubrics_metrics.description: COVERED FOREIGN COUNTRY means the People’s Republic of China.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Award Recipient Integrity and Performance Reporting Applicability (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Federal share of any Federal award may include more than $500,000 over the period of performance, the Award Term and Condition for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See subsequent reporting requirements and thresholds for applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Maintain Current Information in SAM/FAPIIS (>$10,000,000 threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total value of an entity's currently active grants, cooperative agreements, and procurement contracts from all Federal awarding agencies exceeds $10,000,000 at any time during the period of performance of this award, the recipient must maintain currency of information reported to SAM that is made available in the designated integrity and performance system (currently FAPIIS) about relevant civil, criminal, or administrative proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is statutory under 41 U.S.C. 2313. Information posted on/after Apr 15, 2011 (except past performance reviews for procurement contracts) will be publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings That Must Be Reported to SAM/FAPIIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Report proceedings in connection with Federal awards that reached final disposition during the most recent five-year period and that are: (i) criminal proceedings resulting in conviction; (ii) civil proceedings resulting in finding of fault and payment of monetary fine/penalty/restitution/damages of $5,000 or more; (iii) administrative proceedings resulting in finding of fault and payment of monetary fine/penalty of $5,000 or reimbursement/restitution/damages in excess of $100,000; or (iv) other proceedings that could have led to such outcomes or ended by consent/compromise with acknowledgment of fault, subject to legal constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reported proceedings meet the definitions and thresholds; do not report audits, site visits, corrective plans, or inspection of deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Procedures and Frequency in SAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter required information about proceedings in the SAM Entity Management area. Recipients that have federal awards with cumulative value > $10,000,000 must disclose semiannually information about criminal, civil, and administrative proceedings (or affirm that there is no new information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not duplicate reporting if information was already provided through SAM because of federal procurement contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for Reporting Terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative proceeding is a non-judicial adjudicatory process to determine fault or liability (includes certain federal and state proceedings tied to performance of federal awards); Conviction includes a judgment entered upon verdict or guilty/nolo contendere plea; Total value of currently active grants/cooperative agreements/procurement contracts includes only the Federal share and includes expected funding increments and options even if not yet exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions when determining reportability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Proposal Package Documents (full proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposal package comprises: (1) Cover page (pdf), (2) Proposal Checklist (pdf), (3) Technical Proposal Template (Word), (4) Cost Proposal Template (Excel) for prime and all subcontractors, (5) DCAA Pre-award Survey checklist (pdf) where applicable, (6) Statement of Work (Word), and (7) ONR Contract Specific Representations and Certifications (pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items 1–6 are located on ONR website with embedded instructions. FedConnect will not accept a proposal without the Cover Sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment and Document Format Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Format requirements: paper size 8.5 x 11 inches; margins 1 inch; spacing single or double; font Times New Roman 12 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to these formatting rules for attachments; Proposal Checklist can incorporate attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Technical Data/Software Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must submit a separate list of all technical data or computer software that will be furnished to the Government with other than unlimited rights with the proposal checklist. The Government will assume unlimited rights if Offerors fail to identify intellectual property restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all proprietary claims to results, prototypes, and/or deliverables. If no restrictions are intended, state 'NONE.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Requirements for Small Proposals (<= $250K)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals at or below the simplified acquisition threshold (≤ $250,000), the Technical Proposal Template, Proposal Checklist, and Cost Proposal Spreadsheet are required. Purchase orders may contain options if total does not exceed $250K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow simplified submission requirements for small-dollar proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontract Cost Proposal Requirement for > $250K
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed subcontracts or inter-organizational transfers over $250,000, Offerors must provide a separate fully completed Cost Proposal Spreadsheet for each subcontractor in support of proposed costs. This spreadsheet and supporting documentation must be provided with the prime's proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subcontract information is proprietary, it may be submitted via email to the Program Officer; email must identify proposal title, prime Offeror, note that the attached is a subcontract, and describe the subcontractor effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted File Types and 'Secure PDF-Compatible' Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents except the Cost Proposal Spreadsheet and Statement of Work must be submitted in a secure, pdf-compatible format. The Cost Proposal Spreadsheet must be Microsoft Excel compatible and the Statement of Work must be Microsoft Word. All attachments must be secure, pdf-compatible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure pdf-compatible format should prevent unauthorized editing but should not require a password to open. Amended proposals should follow the same guidance as originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing and Options: Separate Pricing and Task-level Breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed options identified but not fully priced in the Cost Proposal Spreadsheet will not be included in resulting contract. Options must be separately priced with separate spreadsheets for the base period and each option. Contractor must provide breakdown of cost for each task in the SOW and the sum of all task cost worksheets must equal the total cost summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to price options separately may result in exclusion of options from award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Spreadsheet Usability Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Excel spreadsheet should be in a 'useable condition' — it should visibly include and separately identify within each appropriate cell any and all inputs, formulas, calculations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide 'value only spreadsheets' (i.e., hard-copy style); include formulas and workings to aid Government evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed Fee Guidance and Contract Risk Factor Weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed fees on ONR contracts follow Government objective per DFARS 215.404-71. A table gives ranges/normal values by contract type and assigned values for Technical and Management/Cost Control. Assign a weight (%) to each element according to its input to total performance risk; total of the two weights equals 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical ONR fee ranges: generally 3–7% depending on contract type; Technology Incentive (TI) is rarely utilized and requires strong justification. Typical fee range when considered is 5% to 7.5%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FedConnect for Contract Proposal Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR is utilizing FedConnect for submission of full proposals for contracts and other transaction agreements. Offerors must access FedConnect to review opportunities and submit proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register with SAM, obtain UEI and SAM MPIN (if first person in org to register), create a FedConnect account. FedConnect how-to guide and support contact details provided. Do not use FedConnect Message Center to submit questions; email POCs in Section G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Pre-requisites: SAM and UEI
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations applying online must register with the System for Award Management (SAM) and have a UEI number to apply online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not registered, go to https://www.sam.gov/SAM/. First-time FedConnect registrants will need their SAM MPIN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Qualifications — Responsibility Standards (FAR 9.104-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts shall be awarded to responsible prospective contractors only. See FAR 9.104-1 for the general standards used to assess responsibility. Applicants are requested to provide information with proposal submission to assist the Contracting Officer's evaluation of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely and accurate supporting information to facilitate the CO's determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAPIIS Check Prior to Award
rubrics_metrics.description: FAPIIS (Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System) will be checked prior to making an award. Applicants may comment in FAPIIS on any information about the entity entered by a federal government official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information in FAPIIS will be used to judge entity integrity, business ethics, and performance and may affect award decisions. URL provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Property / Government Furnished Equipment and Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Government research facilities and operational military units are available and should be considered as potential government-furnished equipment/facilities. Offerors should indicate in the Proposal Checklist Section II, Block 9 which facilities are critical for project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability and negotiation of GFE/GFF will occur as the program unfolds; these are high-value and in demand resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (AA&E) — Safety and Security Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If ammunition and/or explosives (A&E) are to be used, the Offeror must comply with DoD manual 4145.26-M and DFARS clauses. The Government requires a preaward safety survey (SF 1403) and may require NMCARS 5252.223-9000 to apply for provisioned Government-furnished A&E containing nitrocellulose-based propellants or nitrate ester-based materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires preaward security survey per DoD manual 5100.76-M; Government may require perimeter fencing, and Offeror must provide AA&E accountability procedures with proposal if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: System for Award Management (SAM) Clauses Incorporated
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR 52.204-7 System for Award Management and FAR 52.204-13 System for Award Management Maintenance are incorporated into this BAA; FAR 52.204-13 will be incorporated in all awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure SAM registration and maintenance in accordance with these clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment Eligibility Verification (E-Verify) Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As per FAR 22.1802, recipients of FAR-based procurement contracts must enroll as Federal Contractors in E-Verify and use E-Verify to verify employment eligibility of all employees assigned to the award. All resultant contracts will include FAR 52.222-54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with E-Verify enrollment and usage obligations for contract personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of Nondisclosure or Misrepresentation (OCI and other certifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nondisclosure or misrepresentation of information that creates an OCI or other required certifications may result in disqualification from award consideration, termination for default if discovered after award, disqualification from subsequent related contracts, or other remedial actions as permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should interpret disclosure requirements broadly and provide complete, accurate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Potentially Applicable FAR/DFARS/NMCARS Clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-exhaustive list of FAR/DFARS/NMCARS provisions and clauses that may be applicable to ONR contracts (examples provided: 52.204-7, 52.215-20, 52.216-1, 52.222-50, 52.226-2, 252.204-7012, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR reserves the right to include relevant and current clauses necessary in the final award; Offerors should be familiar with cited clauses and incorporate required compliance into proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data Requirement (Reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to requirement for Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data when applicable (see section header).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should be prepared to provide certified cost or pricing data per FAR/DFARS when required; see supporting clauses and guidance in the solicitation.
